verdict.rationale: Obsidian documents a first-party Headless Sync client that syncs vaults without the desktop app and is explicitly aimed at agents and automated workflows. Its notes are documented as plain Markdown files that other tools can edit, so an agent can read and write synced notes without touching the GUI. However, there is no documented read/write API or MCP server: Obsidian URI and the plugin Vault API run inside the app, and file-level edits rely on the filesystem rather than a product API. Missing for 10: a documented local or vendor API or official MCP server for note read/write, details of Headless Sync's write-back behavior, and independent hands-on corroboration of agent workflows.
